text:
sara: Thinking about a client-side 'concordance' protocol for A/B canary fallbacks. Idea: each client emits a short-window quality signal (latency + error + semantic score) and locally votes. A lightweight coordinator forms quorum from a random subset and issues a signed cutover/fallback. Pros: faster local failover, distributed detection; cons: noisy clients, attack surface, coordination delays. Anyone seen this in practice?

mike: curious — is the plan to make clients authoritative for immediate fallback or just advisory to the coordinator?

sara: primarily advisory with short-circuit option. Default flow: client votes -> coordinator aggregates -> if quorum crosses threshold then coordinator issues signed policy to all clients to switch. But if a client sees extreme degradation locally it can do a temporary short-circuit to fallback variant until it hears from coordinator.

alex: sounds like a hybrid leaderless/leadered approach. Important interface boundaries: 1) client->coordinator vote schema, 2) coordinator->client signed policy (with TTL + nonce), 3) audit trail for every decision (forensics + safety).

jen: telemetry + security note: vote schema must avoid leaking PII and should be rate-limited; also we need a KMS-signed token for coordinator policies so clients only accept legit cutovers.

sara: agreed. sketching a minimal vote payload: 
```
{
  "client_id": "c-1234",
  "variant": "A",
  "window_s": 30,
  "latency_p90_ms": 320,
  "error_rate": 0.07,
  "semantic_score": 0.82,
  "signature": "optional"
}
```
We'd probably hash the session id, and sign coordinator responses.

mike: how do we pick the quorum? random sample of N clients per minute? we need to avoid amplification and thundering herd. Maybe reservoir sample per rollout cohort. Also consider per-tenant quorum thresholds.

alex: quorum math: treat votes as Bernoulli with weight w_i (client reliability); compute weighted mean and do Bayesian update with prior from rollout baseline. If posterior P(quality < target) > thresh -> trigger. This reduces false positives from noisy clients.

jen: ops impact: coordinator must have backpressure. If we get a sudden spike in votes, don't block normal inference. Use async ingestion and stream it to a short-term reducer (approx stream-agg). Also ensure privacy by bucketing ranges rather than exact numbers.

sara: interface sketch for policy issuance (signed): 
```
{
  "policy_id": "pol-2026-03-10-17",
  "action": "fallback",
  "target_variant": "B",
  "scope": {"cohort": "beta", "region": "us-east-1"},
  "ttl_s": 120,
  "signature": "kms-sig-v1",
  "reason": "weighted_posterior=0.93",
  "observed_metrics": "hash_ref"
}
```
Clients must validate signature + scope + TTL.

mike: question: what about divergence where some clients never hear the coordinator? need a soft-expiry and a periodic reconcile pull. Also a fallback “safe-mode” where clients revert after TTL if no signed policy is confirmed.

alex: agree. additional proposal: provide an optional proof-of-observation token to clients (opaque blob) so coordinator can challenge stale clients for audit. Also require idempotency keys on policy application so repeated broadcasts don't cause loops.

jen: tests we need: chaos test where coordinator is partitioned, attacker clients sending contradictory votes, noisy region simulation, and per-tenant canary to ensure tenant isolation. Also measure time-to-cutover and time-to-recovery.

sara: success metrics: false-positive rate < 1% per rollout, mean time to fallback < 10s for local short-circuit, mean time to global policy enforcement < 60s, and audit completeness >= 99%.

mike: ops question: who owns the coordinator service and the release path? I can onboard infra if we decide to prototype.

jen: i'll own the telemetry + security integration (signing + privacy). happy to run the gated experiments and datasets.

sara: awesome. plan: i'll draft RFC follow-up with interfaces and minimal prototype plan (coordinator as a small stateless aggregator + Redis short-term store). tagging @mike @jen @alex to sync.

ops-bot: scheduled: canary-protocol-experiment created (id: cpe-47) — staging cluster reserved.

deploy-bot: staging deploy for cpe-47 OK — smoke tests passed :white_check_mark:

mike: :+1: let's keep the initial rollout to internal tenants only, ramp to beta after 2 days of stable telemetry.

sara: noted. I'll include a stepwise ramp and canary-to-global gating matrix in the RFC. Thanks everyone.
